subject.title: feat(fleet): multi-tenant hosting via openclaw fleet cell supervisor

question: Should OpenClaw core own this privileged fleet lifecycle supervisor after the branch, persistence, and port-allocation defects are corrected?
rationale: A corrected implementation would still create a permanent first-party security, operations, upgrade, and support boundary; the linked issue review recommended external orchestration unless maintainers explicitly sponsor core ownership.

options.title: External orchestration contract
options.body: Define and document a hardened, complete cell persistence and isolation contract while leaving privileged lifecycle management to established orchestration systems.

options.title: Approve core fleet ownership
options.body: Sponsor the reconstructed and corrected supervisor after security-owner approval and real Docker/Podman lifecycle proof.

options.title: Narrow to contract foundations
options.body: Land only reusable cell-profile and trust-model foundations while deferring the registry and destructive lifecycle commands.

recommendation.title: External orchestration contract
recommendation.body: Define and document a hardened, complete cell persistence and isolation contract while leaving privileged lifecycle management to established orchestration systems.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the canonical proposal and implementation and has the strongest current-main history across the affected Docker, state, and security surfaces.
